title: Filters and ultrafilters: large subsets, maximality, and examples
summary: Consistent notions of large subsets extend to ultrafilters that decide every complement pair.
abstract: A filter is a consistent way to call some subsets large: enlarging a large set keeps it large, and intersecting two large sets keeps both conditions together. An ultrafilter extends this idea by choosing exactly one of each subset and its complement. Assuming the axiom of choice, every filter can be extended to an ultrafilter. On the natural numbers, this gives ultrafilters that treat all sets with finitely many exceptions as large and contain no finite set, so their choices do not concentrate on any single point.
